target.title: fix(commitments): avoid quadratic heartbeat session discovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where heartbeat commitment fan-out scans the complete commitments JSON store once for every qualifying due record. When many due records belong to one session, that quadratic work runs under the commitments queue/file lock and increases heartbeat latency. The prior isolated medians were approximately 191 ms at 1,000 records, 847 ms at 2,000, and 2.28 s at 4,000.

## Why This Change Was Made

The commitments store now builds the rolling 24-hour sent-count map once per agent and reuses it for due-session discovery and single-session due selection. The due-window, snooze, expiry, daily-cap, ordering, limit, agent-scope, queue, and cross-process file-lock behavior remain on the existing path.

This is intentionally an interim JSON-store fix. OpenClaw's shared SQLite state schema already contains a commitments table and indexes, but making it canonical requires a separate JSON-to-SQLite migration/doctor contract and broader persistence coverage. That migration remains a follow-up rather than expanding this focused latency fix.

## User Impact

Heartbeat commitment discovery changes from repeated full-store counting to one aggregation pass plus the existing due-record scan. Large concentrated sessions therefore scale linearly with store size instead of quadratically, without changing which sessions are eligible for delivery.

## Evidence

- Added a correctness test covering due-window filtering, snoozes, rolling daily caps, agent scope, and sorted session keys.
- Added a concentrated-session scaling test with 8,000 due records in one session and one recent sent record. It exercises the public `listDueCommitmentSessionKeys` interface, asserts the expected session, and enforces a 2,000 ms bound. The local fallback run reported 11/11 tests passed and 1.02 s in the test body.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `oxfmt --check src/commitments/store.ts src/commitments/store.test.ts` passed.
- `oxlint src/commitments/store.ts src/commitments/store.test.ts` passed.
- Fresh local autoreview: `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine codex --thinking high` — clean.
- Fresh post-commit branch autoreview against `origin/main`: `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --engine codex --thinking high` — clean.
- The approved Blacksmith remote backend was unavailable because the local Blacksmith client is unauthenticated. The narrow local `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commitments/store.test.ts` fallback was used with the existing dependency cache; exact-head GitHub CI remains the remote validation gate.

## AI-Assisted Disclosure

This PR was prepared with Codex and is AI-assisted. I reviewed the implementation, its callers, sibling selection path, persistence/locking behavior, tests, and the SQLite/Kysely storage contracts.
